claims.text: Inducing controlled, stepwise coherent carbide nanoprecipitations in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys will enhance heat-transfer capability.
Coherent carbide nanoprecipitations will preserve or improve structural integrity under cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
A controlled thermo-mechanical process can produce stepwise coherent carbide nanoprecipitations uniformly dispersed in the matrix.
The proposed dual improvement should hold during thermal cycling and static mechanical loading from 800°C to 1200°C.
Temperatures of 800°C to 1200°C and the proposed loads mimic operating conditions for plasma-facing intermediate components.
The induced carbide nanoprecipitates will be coherent and form strong interfacial bonds with the matrix.
Carbide nanoprecipitates will establish continuous thermally conductive pathways across grain boundaries.
These pathways will enhance phonon conduction across grain boundaries.
These pathways will enhance electron conduction across grain boundaries.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will impede dislocation motion.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces will reduce susceptibility to crack initiation.
Coherent carbide nanoprecipitates will reinforce the alloy against crack propagation.
The treated alloy will have significantly higher effective thermal conductivity than the baseline alloy.
The treated alloy will have fracture toughness equal to or greater than that of the baseline alloy.
The treated alloy will have equal or improved mechanical stability under high-temperature cyclic loading.
A tungsten-based refractory HEA without induced carbide nanoprecipitates typically has lower thermal conductivity.
A tungsten-based refractory HEA without induced carbide nanoprecipitates may undergo microstructural degradation during cyclic high-temperature exposure.
Excessive precipitate coarsening may compromise both thermal and mechanical performance.
